docs.title: ListHoard
docs.text: Self-hosted browser and one-click importer for public movie/TV lists. Seven providers sync daily into one local, deduplicates catalog; every poster is cached on disk; any browsed list imports into Radarr or Sonarr with the arrs' full add-options surface; every import can be un-imported.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Empty by design — the app ships with no bundled lists; you paste a list URL and it syncs from there.
  • Polite sync — per-provider hour/day request budgets; a throttled source pauses and shows used/limit on the health board, rather than erroring.
  • Curation first — imports are the rows you checked, never a bulk grab.
  • Anime is first-class — anime-flagged lists import into Sonarr with seriesType = anime.
  • Explicit content stays off — the adult module does not even register unless you set LISTHOARD_ENABLE_XXX=on yourself.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Everything lives in .env — copy .env.example from the repo root and fill. Real secrets never go in a committed file; the example file carries placeholders only.

docs.title: Required
docs.text: Key Meaning TMDB_API_KEY Free TMDB v3 key — the only must-have POSTGRES_HOST / POSTGRES_PORT / POSTGRES_USER / POSTGRES_PASSWORD / POSTGRES_DB Your postgres, or the fullstack overlay's embedded one (POSTGRES_HOST=postgres) TZ IANA timezone, e.g. Europe/Berlin

docs.title: Your arrs (optional — imports need one)
docs.text: Key Meaning RADARR_BASE_URL / RADARR_API_KEY Radarr for movies SONARR_BASE_URL / SONARR_API_KEY Sonarr for shows

docs.title: Your Jellyfin (optional — powers auth + badges)
docs.text: Key Meaning JELLYFIN_BASE_URL / JELLYFIN_API_KEY Jellyfin gives in-library badges and, in jellyfin auth mode, the account system to log in with. Absent = degraded badges, not broken pages.

docs.title: Auth modes
docs.text: Key Meaning LISTHOARD_AUTH_MODE jellyfin | local | token. Empty = the first-run setup decides. LISTHOARD_ADMIN_TOKEN Shared secret for token mode LISTHOARD_LOCAL_ADMIN_USER / LISTHOARD_LOCAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD Credentials for local mode

docs.title: Behaviour knobs
docs.text: Key Default Meaning LISTHOARD_SEED_ON_BOOT off The curated starter loads by explicit choice (a first-run option), never automatically — a fresh instance ships an empty catalog LISTHOARD_ENABLE_XXX off Explicit-content module: when off, the module is not registered, the toggle never renders, and the adult import flow is absent entirely LISTHOARD_HUGE_LIST_THRESHOLD 5000 Imports of lists above this default to search-on-add off (still per-import overridable) LISTHOARD_BUDGET_<SLUG>_PER_HOUR documented quota Per-provider request budget, hour window — slugs: tmdb, trakt, mdblist, and each scraper LISTHOARD_BUDGET_<SLUG>_PER_DAY documented quota Same, day window LISTHOARD_SLOW_REQUEST_MS 1000 Warn when a page render exceeds this LISTHOARD_SLOW_QUERY_MS 500 Warn when a database statement exceeds this

docs.title: Optional provider keys
docs.text: Key Meaning TRAKT_CLIENT_ID Trakt reads (public lists only) MDBLIST_API_KEY MDBList export path TVDB_API_KEY / TVDB_SUBSCRIPTION_PIN Only if driving TVDB v4 instead of the scrape fallback

docs.title: Providers
docs.text:
ListHoard pulls lists from these providers. Each one walks the same adapter interface: authenticate, enumerate, fetch, map items to (media type, TMDB id, TVDB id) rows.

Provider Access Key needed? Notes TMDB Official API v3 Yes — the only must-have (free signup) List + collection + trending endpoints Trakt Official API, client id only Optional Public list reads need no OAuth MDBList Official export per user/list Optional Same export contract the arr import-list pipeline uses; degrades to "source unavailable" on the health board without a key Letterboxd Scrape (no public API) No robots-respecting, adaptive pacing, backoff IMDb Scrape of list/chart pages + public datasets No IMDb ids translate to TMDB/TVDB once, cached Rotten Tomatoes Scrape of awards/rank pages No Structure drifts often; the health board catches it TVDB API v4 or scrape fallback Optional Researched at bring-up; falls back to scraping that provider's curated rank pages if the v4 pin model blocks

docs.title: Keys and degradation
docs.text:
• TMDB is the only required key — a fresh free signup takes about a minute; the in-app setup links the signup page directly.
  • Trakt, MDBList and TVDB keys are optional: without one, the provider works key-less where that is possible, or reports "source unavailable" honestly on the health board. A missing key never produces placeholder demo data.
  • Scraped providers (Letterboxd, IMDb, Rotten Tomatoes) need no key at all.
  • If you enable the explicit-content module (LISTHOARD_ENABLE_XXX=on), its scraped adult-list provider joins the queue as a standard adapter; left off, nothing adult is registered, rendered or routed — the UI toggle never renders and the adult flow is absent from the app entirely.

docs.title: Politeness
docs.text: Every request a source makes passes through a per-provider budget (LISTHOARD_BUDGET_<SLUG>_PER_HOUR / _PER_DAY; per-provider defaults sit at each API's documented quota and ship in the compose file's comments). When a budget is spent, the source pauses — it is reported on the health board with used/limit and resumes in the next window; it is never marked failing. Scraped providers honour robots.txt with a 1 req/s adaptive floor and exponential backoff.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom-first, one command each.

Symptom First check Dashboard empty, nothing added docker compose logs listhoard right after your first sync — a source that failed to fetch names its error on the health board, which the dashboard renders A source shows budget exhausted Expected honest pause, not an error: the source hit its per-provider request budget and will resume in the next window. Raise the window's ceiling via LISTHOARD_BUDGET_<SLUG>_PER_HOUR if your quota allows A source shows unavailable That provider's optional key is missing or invalid; check Providers for which key applies A scrape source stays stale after a site change Expected: structural break quarantines that one source and the board names the last error; other sources continue; the stale contents stay visible until the next successful sync Import button does nothing Check the arr is reachable and RADARR_BASE_URL / SONARR_BASE_URL respond from inside the container; the import dialog names the lookup failure per row Login fails Auth mode mismatch — see Configuration; token mode needs LISTHOARD_ADMIN_TOKEN, local mode needs LISTHOARD_LOCAL_ADMIN_* Page loads slow Tune both warning thresholds: LISTHOARD_SLOW_REQUEST_MS / LISTHOARD_SLOW_QUERY_MS; the logs carry the explicit slow request / slow query lines past them

docs.title: Container won't start
docs.text:
docker compose logs listhoard | tail -50
  1. .env missing a required key — check the compose file's required list.
  2. Postgres unreachable — docker compose logs postgres if you run the fullstack overlay; else verify POSTGRES_HOST from the container's network.
  3. Port already in use — change LISTHOARD_PORT (or the quickstart's mapped 8675).

docs.title: Health endpoint
docs.text: GET /healthz returns {"status": "ok", "catalog_items": N}; anything else is the app telling you, not a guess.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text: The app follows semver: 0.x is the shippability ramp; 1.0.0 marks public readiness. Releases land as GitHub releases with per-release notes.

docs.title: Update
docs.text:
git pull
docker compose build && docker compose up -d
# fullstack overlay:
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.fullstack.yml build
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.fullstack.yml up -d

docs.title: What carries over
docs.text:
• Your catalog and import history live in postgres — for the fullstack overlay that is the pg-data named volume; keep it backed up if import history matters to you (the catalog rebuilds from the sources; the import history does not).
  • The image cache lives in the listhoard-images volume — nothing to migrate, it repopulates on demand if ever lost.

docs.title: Breaking changes
docs.text: A 0.x bump that changes a .env key's meaning or a compose shape calls it out in the release notes and in CHANGELOG.md. Check the notes before git pull when you have a long-lived deployment; the app version at any commit is in the release tag.
